I've been working these 7 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. With my agricultural college background, I tend to think in terms of target yields and nutrient rates — but I've also learned that on a small farm like mine, cash flow and labor availability constrain everything. I'm 59, my wife helps when she can, and my son and his wife work in a factory over in Handan and send money home. That remittance means I'm not as cash-strapped as some neighbors, but I still watch every yuan. I hire a bit of labor during the harvest and planting rushes when the window is narrow, especially for that tight wheat-to-maize turnaround in June.

For winter wheat, I'm planting around October 12th with an improved Jimai variety — I've used it for five years and it performs reliably on my land. I'm targeting about 480 kg per mu. My base fertilizer is 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer broadcast before sowing, which gives me roughly 7.5 kg N, 7.5 kg P₂O₅, and 7.5 kg K₂O per mu. Then at jointing in late March, I'll topdress with 20 kg per mu of urea, adding another 9 kg N. That's about 16.5 kg N total per mu. I know some of the bigger business farms push higher, but on my 7 mu I've found that going much beyond this doesn't pay back reliably in dry years. I'll irrigate three times: a winter irrigation in late November to prevent winter kill, one at jointing, and one at grain filling in early May. The pumping costs add up — about 25 yuan per mu each time — but skipping the grain-filling irrigation has cost me more in lost yield than it saves in electricity. For pesticides, I'll apply herbicide, and I'll monitor for powdery mildew and rust. If the spring turns wet, I'll add a fungicide, but I don't spray it automatically. That's wasted money if the weather stays dry.

Summer maize is always a race against the calendar. I harvest wheat around June 8th, and I need the maize in the ground by June 12th at the latest. I'll plant a hybrid Zhengdan variety, about 2.5 kg per mu. Because of that tight window, I apply 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting — roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 6 kg K₂O — and if I have time and the weather cooperates, I'll side-dress urea at the 8-leaf stage to bring total N to about 15 kg per mu. If I'm too busy or the soil is too dry, I skip the side-dress; the base rate is usually enough for my yield target of 500 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice: once if it's dry at planting to get the seed germinated, and once in late August during grain filling if the rains don't come. I always use herbicide for maize — the weeds would choke it otherwise — and I watch for corn borer. I only spray insecticide if I actually see damage or eggs, because preventive spraying on a 7-mu farm is just money down the drain.

Total input costs this year will run about 5,500 yuan. I could spend another 800 yuan on extra fertilizer and another irrigation to maybe push yields a bit higher, but I'd rather keep that cash in reserve. My grandson starts middle school next year, and on a small farm, having liquidity for family emergencies matters more than squeezing out every last kilogram.
